questions.question: Name four kinds of sources that tell us about the San and Khoikhoi and give an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Stories, such as the San stories recorded by Bleek and Lloyd in the 1870s; objects, such as stone tools and the shell beads from Blombos Cave; rock paintings, such as paintings of eland and hunters in caves; and books, such as the diaries and descriptions written by European sailors and settlers.

questions.question: Why must historians be careful when using books written by European settlers about the Khoikhoi and San?
questions.expected_answer: The writers often did not speak their languages or understand their customs, some looked down on them and described them unfairly, and some wrote to persuade others to take the land. These sources may be biased, so historians ask who wrote them, when and why.

questions.question: Explain why it is better to use many sources than just one.
questions.expected_answer: Each kind of source has strengths and weaknesses. When several different sources, such as a story, an object and a painting, point to the same thing, historians can be more confident that it is true.
